questions.stem: What pivotal question lies at the core of incrementality in marketing?
options: Which advertising channel is cheapest?
Would customers buy without the corresponding paid advertising?
How many ads should be shown per day?
Which creative design performs best?
How large should the marketing budget be?
questions.explanation: Incrementality is built on the question of whether customers would purchase a product or service without paid advertising.

questions.stem: Into how many groups does incrementality analysis divide audience reactions to ads?
options: Two
Four
Three
Five
Six
questions.explanation: Audiences are divided into three groups: non-responsive, pre-existing demand and incremental.

questions.stem: Which audience group is unaffected by ads no matter how much they see them?
options: Incremental audience
Pre-existing demand audience
Control group
Non-responsive audience
Exposed audience
questions.explanation: The non-responsive audience does not engage or buy because of ads, regardless of how much they see them.

questions.stem: How does the pre-existing demand audience respond to ads?
options: They never buy, with or without ads
They buy only because they saw an ad
They ignore all marketing channels
They switch to a competitor's product
They were already planning to buy; ads might change when they buy but not whether they buy
questions.explanation: People with pre-existing demand were already planning to buy; ads might change the timing but will not change their mind about buying.

questions.stem: Which audience group engages or buys only because they saw ads?
options: Incremental audience
Non-responsive audience
Pre-existing demand audience
Loyal audience
Organic audience
questions.explanation: The incremental audience is directly affected by ads: these customers engage or buy only because they saw them.

questions.stem: How is an incrementality test structured?
options: One group sees ads at different times of day
Group A is exposed to advertising and Group B is not, with both groups otherwise as identical as possible
Two groups are shown different products
A single group is surveyed about their purchase intent
Ads are shown only to previous customers
questions.explanation: Incrementality tests compare Group A, exposed to advertising, with Group B, not exposed, keeping the groups identical in every other respect.

questions.stem: Which metrics are evaluated when comparing the two groups after an incrementality test?
options: Page load time and bounce rate
Employee headcount and payroll
Conversion rates, order rates and revenue per user
Number of ads shown and ad size
Social media followers and likes
questions.explanation: Businesses determine the actual impact of advertising by evaluating conversion rates, order rates and revenue per user across the two groups.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of identifying the audience directly influenced by ads?
options: To exclude them from future campaigns
To charge them higher prices
To reduce the total number of customers
To optimise resources efficiently and maximise the impact of advertising efforts
To replace paid advertising with organic content
questions.explanation: Targeting the audience directly affected by ads lets marketers direct resources where they maximise advertising impact, driving ongoing growth.

questions.stem: Which statement about the non-responsive audience is correct?
options: They buy earlier when shown more ads
They are the main source of incremental revenue
They are the exposed group in an incrementality test
They respond best to email marketing
Ads do not make them feel like engaging or buying
questions.explanation: The non-responsive audience does not feel like engaging or buying because of ads, however often they see them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three audience groups in incrementality analysis?
options: Price-sensitive audience
Non-responsive audience
Pre-existing demand audience
Incremental audience
People who buy only because they saw ads
questions.explanation: The three groups are non-responsive, pre-existing demand and incremental (those who buy only because of ads); a price-sensitive group is not one of them.
